meta.method: Daily 7-day flood-risk forecast. No weather model is run here: published forecasts are combined with FloodTrace's own satellite-rain history. The ECMWF IFS 0.25 deg ensemble (control + 50 members) is fetched once for all 68 IMERG 0.1 deg cells (one multi-coordinate call; the model grid is coarser than the cells, so several cells share one model point) and drives the headline rain numbers; the GFS 0.25 deg ensemble is stored as a second opinion. Since Task 44 every ECMWF member's daily total is first calibrated to Lagos rain by a quantile mapping fitted per lead day on the 2024-2026 hindcast (events/forecast/calibration.json, built by pipeline/calibrate.py), and each member's hourly values are scaled by the same daily factor, so the medians, percentiles, chances, risk windows and the hourly export are IMERG-equivalent; raw_median_mm keeps the uncalibrated median beside the calibrated one, and the GFS second opinion stays uncalibrated. Per cell and Lagos day the pipeline records the ensemble-median and 90th-percentile 24-h rain, the chance of at least 20/40/60 mm (share of the 51 series), the peak 3-hour window, the hours at risk (member-median rate at least 10 mm/h, or at least 30% of members at it), whether those hours come within 2 h of an EOT20 high tide, a plain risk level (chance of heavy rain, nudged by this cell's own reported-flood record), and, at medium or above, past days whose rain matched the forecast (analogues). Each cell also carries the 168-hour member-median and 90th-percentile rain rate in mm/h for the UI. GloFAS river ensembles and their 1984-present daily-flow history are fetched for two river points, and each forecast day is flagged when the member-median flow reaches the point's historical 90th/99th percentile. Raw API responses are cached under pipeline/cache/forecast/2026-11-10/ (ecmwf_ifs025.json, flood_ogun-ishi_ensemble.json, flood_ogun-ishi_history.json, flood_owo-ikorodu_ensemble.json, flood_owo-ikorodu_history.json, gfs025.json) and reused on same-day reruns, so an archived run stays reproducible.

calibration.method: Quantile mapping per lead day (1-7), fitted by pipeline/calibrate.py on the 2024-2026 hindcast (ECMWF IFS 0.25 deg deterministic runs vs IMERG daily totals), pooling all 68 cells; no per-cell adjustment (tested and unstable across seasons). Every ECMWF member's daily total is mapped to IMERG-equivalent mm BEFORE chances, levels, risk windows and the hourly export are computed; each member's hourly values are scaled by that member's same daily factor. median_mm is calibrated; raw_median_mm keeps the uncalibrated median beside it. The GFS second opinion is NOT calibrated (the mapping was fitted on ECMWF IFS runs). Validated leave-one-season-out: the calibrated day-1 p99 matches IMERG's (54.4 vs 53.9 mm, model raw 28.9), and flood days flagged at 40 mm went from 1 of 19 (raw) to 6 of 19 (calibrated) — but most flagged days still pass without a reported flood, and with 19 flood days the gain may be noise.
calibration.fit_period: 2024-04-01 to 2026-10-21 (2024, 2025, 2026), April-November; deployed mapping refit on all seasons, validation leave-one-season-out

level_rule.rule: A cell-day whose CALIBRATED member-median reaches 15 mm is raised to at least 'medium', whatever the ensemble chances say. The threshold was fixed on the 2024 and 2025 seasons only (each calibrated by a mapping fitted on the other season), as the day-1 threshold with the best true skill statistic TSS = POD - POFD over the candidates 15/20/25/30/35/40 mm; it was frozen before the 2026 test season was looked at. It is 'applied' only when it differs from the 40 mm the chance ladder already uses.
level_rule.criterion: max TSS = POD - POFD at day 1, citywide day-level flags

trust.design: Out of sample, leave-one-season-out over 2024-2026: each season's numbers come from a mapping fitted without it (2024 and 2025 from a mapping fitted on the other of the two, 2026 from one fitted on 2024+2025). The threshold itself was fixed on 2024+2025 before the 2026 numbers were computed.

models.rivers: GloFAS via the Open-Meteo Flood API (control + 50 perturbed members)
models.tide: EOT20 (17 constituents), from the precomputed tide table (events/forecast/tide_table.json)

rules.risk_window: An hour is inside the risk window when the member-median rain rate is at least 10 mm/h, or at least 30% of the 51 ensemble series reach 10 mm/h in that hour; consecutive hours are joined into ranges in Lagos time. A day's window is flagged near_high_tide when any of its hours falls within +/- 2 h of a high tide.
rules.hourly_rate_justification: 10 mm/h is the low end of what preceded reported flood days in the satellite record: on each of the 87 reported flood days, the highest 30-min IMERG rain rate over all 68 cells on the day itself or the day before has a 10th percentile of 8.9 mm/h and a median of 21.9 mm/h, and 74 of 87 days reached 10 mm/h somewhere in the city. Hourly ensemble precipitation (mm per hour) is compared against that rate directly.
rules.risk_level: The level starts from the chance of heavy rain (high: at least 30% chance of 40 mm in 24 h; medium: at least 10%; low: at least 20% chance of 20 mm; none below that), then moves one step by this cell's own record when it has at least 5 past days of the forecast's size class (10-20 / 20-40 / 40+ mm, April-November of the searched months, 2014 onward): one step up if at least a quarter of those days were reported floods within 5 km of the cell centre, one step down if none of them were. In one sentence: heavy rain likely or possible, checked against how often rain of that size here actually flooded.
rules.calibration: Every ECMWF member's daily rain total is mapped to IMERG-equivalent mm through the quantile mapping in events/forecast/calibration.json (fitted per lead day on the 2024-2026 hindcast, pooled over all cells; a per-cell adjustment was tested and rejected as unstable across seasons). Each member's hourly values are scaled by that member's same daily factor, and everything downstream — chances, levels, risk windows, the hourly export — is computed on the calibrated rain; raw_median_mm keeps the uncalibrated median beside the calibrated one. The GFS second opinion is not calibrated. Level floor: a calibrated member-median of at least 15 mm raises a cell-day to at least medium, whatever the ensemble chances say — the day-1 threshold fixed on the 2024 and 2025 seasons as the best balance of flood days caught against false alarms (TSS, out of sample within those seasons) and kept frozen before the 2026 test season, where it flagged 3 of 8 flood days against 1 of 8 at 40 mm.
rules.analogues: For medium and high cell-days: past days (April-November of the searched months, 2014 onward) whose IMERG 24-h total at the cell is within +/- 25% of the forecast median and at least 20 mm. Days with a flood reported within 5 km of the cell centre come first (flood_day), then the closest to the forecast; up to 5 are kept, each with the reported flood areas within 5 km of the cell centre. Counts: n_qualifying_flood_days = qualifying days with a flood reported within 5 km; n_qualifying_citywide_flood_days = qualifying days with a flood reported anywhere in Lagos.
rules.rivers: Per river point: the daily ensemble median and 90th-percentile flow over the forecast days, flagged at_or_above_p90_hist / at_or_above_p99_hist when the median reaches the historical 90th/99th percentile of daily flow at that point (1984-01-01 onward, GloFAS reanalysis).
rules.tides: The EOT20 astronomical tide is read hourly at the offshore point over the 7 forecast days from the precomputed tide table (events/forecast/tide_table.json, built by pipeline/tide_table.py) when the window is inside it, and computed locally with pyTMD otherwise; every local maximum is listed as a high tide (times to the nearest hour, heights in metres above sea level, rounded to the centimetre). No storm surge, no lagoon damping or phase lag is included.

caveats: A reported flood undercounts real floods: the catalog is news coverage, not a gauge, so floods no outlet reported are missing and every 'how often it flooded' number here is a floor, not the truth.

The calibration corrects how much rain the model forecasts, not where it puts it: out of sample it flagged 6 of 19 flood days at day 1 against 1 of 19 raw, but most flagged days still pass without a reported flood, and with only 19 flood days that gain may be noise (see meta.calibration.trust).
The forecast model is coarser than our history cells: the ECMWF ensemble is 0.25 deg (about 25 km), so several 0.1 deg cells share one model point and neighbourhood rain is smoothed.
The chances are the spread of the model's own ensemble, not true probabilities.
The tide is astronomical only: no storm surge, and the lagoon drains slower than the open sea, so the real high water inside Lagos can be different.
River flow is modelled (GloFAS), not measured; there is no public gauge for the Ogun at Kara or the Osun/Owo outlet.
Forecasts get less reliable further out; by day 7 this is a hint, not a plan.
Satellite rain (IMERG) smooths storm cores, so the heaviest burst in a cell can be heavier than the cell number shows.
